spans.title: The Sword in the Stone
spans.blurb: England has no king, and a sword no lord can budge stands in a churchyard stone. A boy rides back for his brother's forgotten blade.

spans.title: The Banished Magdalene
spans.blurb: A village that stages the Passion has cast out its finest player. On a stormy night she walks the weir plank, and a stranger watches from the shore.

spans.title: Behind the Curtain
spans.blurb: At a dance, a girl who hates parties backs into a curtained nook already occupied by a shy boy from next door.
spans.brokenNote: The final line stops mid sentence, so the reader hits a visible truncation instead of an ending.

spans.title: Anger on Thin Ice
spans.blurb: Amy burns the little book her sister spent years writing. Jo vows never to forgive her, while the last ice of winter waits on the river.

spans.title: An Hour After Midnight
spans.blurb: It is an hour after midnight; a letter has just told a general that his friend is dead. He writes through grief to the one soul that steadies him.

spans.title: Two Minutes for Panting
spans.blurb: At a fashionable spa, the whole town's morning is ruled by one very small man with a monocle, a physician with an enormous watch, and perfect timing.

spans.title: Lilacs at Sunrise
spans.blurb: A guest slips out at dawn to bid goodbye to a borrowed paradise and to the woman who belongs in it. Then a window opens above him.

spans.title: The Doctor's Scar
spans.blurb: A country doctor carries a long scar down his jaw. The story behind it begins with a slip on a rug in a room full of surgical instruments.

spans.title: The Singing House
spans.blurb: Lost on a winter night and unable to recall her friend's name, a girl hears a voice singing inside a dark and empty house.

spans.title: Out of the Wreckage
spans.blurb: A man wakes in the night forest beside a burning plane, with a lump on his head and no memory beyond one blinding flash of light.

spans.title: The Pirates' Chorus
spans.blurb: Two travelers reach a lonely moorland inn where a room full of young gentlemen sings pirate songs. One listener knows exactly what the singing means.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows that Major Helzephron commands the pirate gang, an identity the novel spends its early chapters building toward.
